title: Refuting the distinction of substance through Scripture
english: "...and God was not a stranger among them." Jeremiah likewise says: "And you have not said, 'Where is the Lord, the one who brought you up from the land of Egypt, the one who guided you in the wilderness?'" (Jeremiah 2:19). Isaiah says that the Holy Spirit has guided: "For He led them through the deep, as a horse through the desert without tiring, and as livestock through a field, a spirit came from the Lord and guided them." (Isaiah 43:16). And Paul teaches that Christ has become their guide: "For they drank from a spiritual following rock, and the rock was Christ." (1 Corinthians 10:4). To this, Jude also writes universally: "For once the Lord Jesus, having saved a people out of Egypt, a second time destroyed those who did not believe in Him." (Jude 1:5).

There, therefore, the attempt of those who call the seventh Son and the Divine Spirit a creature is twice refuted, as is the use of 'another hypostasis' as a pretext to mark the one infinite nature as being different, and the claim that 'God was not a stranger among them,' that is to say, of a different substance. In the same manner Moses says: "There shall be no inheritance or lot for the Levites in the land; the Lord Himself is their inheritance." (Numbers 18:20). And Jeremiah says: "He who formed all things is Himself the inheritance of Jacob; the Lord is His name." (Jeremiah 10:7). And David says in the 14th Psalm: "The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup." (Psalm 16:5).

Paul also writes to the Ephesians that the Holy Spirit is the inheritance: "In whom," he says, "having believed, we were sealed with the Spirit of the promise, the Holy [Spirit], who is the pledge of our inheritance." (Ephesians 1:13-14). Similarly, Paul writes to the Corinthians: "There are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit; and there are diversities of ministries, but the same Lord; and there are diversities of activities, but the same God who works all things in all." (1 Corinthians 12:4-11).

By demonstrating the identity of the Divinity, He recalls not only the Spirit first, then the Son, and thus the Father, but also, having just said that God works all things, He leads into: "And all these things works the one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to each one individually as He wills." (1 Corinthians 12:11). He clearly and explicitly presents Him as God, consubstantial with the Father and the Son at once, and as self-determining. One has heard also of God and the Father from Isaiah saying...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Unit 6 rem mid
english: “And I will not give my glory to another” (Isa 42:8); and John said: “that all may honor the Son as they honor the Father” (John 5:23) — for he already knew clearly that glory is referred to the Only-begotten and the Holy Spirit, not to one of different substance. Again, Mark says from Christ: “For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, of him the Son of man will also be ashamed, when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels” (Mark 8:38).

Matthew, setting forth the same passage, did not say “in his Father’s” but “in his Son’s,” writing thus: “But when the Son of man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory” (Matt 25:31). And in John too he says: “Glorify me with the glory which I had with you before the world was” (John 17:5).

20. Concerning the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit dwelling among the faithful because of their consubstantiality and equal power — and against the objection of the heterodox. We will find still further the consubstantiality of the Trinity, and how all things are unchangeably possible to it, if we consider that it alone — being beyond the immaterial and the invisible — can be partaken of in respect of essence and fill the temple it created. And not only does this fact befit it, but also the word: for unchangeability follows on what is partaken of, and on this the uncreated, which is also without beginning. But nothing created — to go by scriptural usage — can be partaken of by way of participation or fill man essentially; only matters of a good or a bad disposition.

title: Unit 6 rem close
english: …of God dwell in you?” and: “Do you not know that your bodies are a temple of the Holy Spirit in you, whom you have from God?” (1 Cor 3:16; 6:19). And to the Ephesians: “that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner man, that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith.” (Eph 3:16-17).

And as when the Master says in John: “the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees him nor knows him; but you know him, because he abides with you and will be in you” (John 14:17). And again: “If anyone loves me, he will keep my word; and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our abode with him” (John 14:23).
And this will be still clearer to the observer: that the almighty divine Word, willing it, both remained unchanged and was carried in the womb by the Virgin.

But they again raise objections, saying: “It is written, allegedly, concerning Ananias: ‘Why has Satan filled your heart?’ (Acts 5:3); and concerning Judas, that ‘Satan entered into him’ (John 13:27).” To them it must be said that he fills the one who does not attend to “Do not let your foot be moved, and he who keeps you will not slumber” (Ps 120:3) — not by being partaken of, nor by riding upon the soul as it were, but by deceiving, and working in the treacherous manner of malice, and making his own wickedness a mere side-show. In the same way he filled Elymas his son with the prompting of a satanic deed. For Paul says to him — being filthy in mind and in deeds and full of devilish wickedness and deceiving the saints, as it seems […].
